text:
ConocoPhillips gained 1.6% today, continuing a sharp rebound from earlier in the week—the stock has climbed 4% over the last three trading days after dropping 7.6% through November 10th. The bounce aligns with a recovery in crude prices: US oil has risen from around $85 to $89.62 per barrel over that same period, which supports energy stocks broadly. The 59% spike in heating oil prices reported today is also relevant to the sector, signaling tighter supply conditions that can support margins for refiners and producers.

However, there's a headwind that hasn't reversed: the International Energy Agency reported that Russian crude production rebounded in October and global oil markets have moved back into surplus (more supply than demand). This longer-term shift toward oversupply is likely why the stock fell 7.6% over the prior week despite today's bounce—the fundamental backdrop for oil has turned less supportive even as short-term prices recovered.
